title: End-to-end user testing of Field Notes: Android, then macOS

spine.active_goal: Verify, by driving the live app the way a normal user would, that every Field Notes feature works on the Galaxy Note 10+ (Android) and then on the Mac, and report defects ranked by user impact. Bounded by the journeys in ~/.mitosis/field-notes/testkit/E2E-TEST-PLAN.md, not by statistical gate counts or open-ended edge cases.
spine.next_step: Finish the interphase spec at docs/specs/android-e2e-defect-fixes.md. Wait for the last scout on search, garden, streak, spell check and accessibility. Then fill sections 1 to 14 of the bug template, embedding the feature-method parts for H3, H5, H10, H11, H12 and H14. Run check_spec.py and the interphase:spec-reviewer agent, get the owner's approval, write docs/specs/android-e2e-defect-fixes.items.json and run check_items.py, verify the tree guard, and hand the spec to mitosis as the owner asked. macOS testing (c3) stays paused until the owner says go.

open_risks.text: The Android app does not build as the repository stands: file_picker 11.0.2 skips its Kotlin plugin on AGP 9 while android/gradle.properties sets android.builtInKotlin=false, and enabling built-in Kotlin breaks audio_session and the other KGP plugins. Test builds must apply testkit/patches/android-probe-build.patch; the real fix is the owner's call and is itself a Blocks finding.

Camera, microphone, photo and notification prompts on the phone need the owner's consent; ask once whether the harness may use adb shell pm grant for the probe package, otherwise the owner taps Allow. Voice, video, photo pick and reminder journeys stall without it.

The probe wraps the app in a second ProviderScope, so ref.exists(appSettingsProvider) is false and spell check never turns on in the probe; judge spell check on the plain app build or a single-scope probe.

The phone has no Google account, so Gboard cannot be installed; keyboard journeys use Samsung Keyboard only. Hardware-keyboard chord cases in the harness assume macOS meanings and should not be read as Android defects.

On macOS the screensaver starts after 30 minutes of owner idle and stops unattended runs; keep-awake (caffeinate tied to the queue, display sleep at the end) needs the owner's approval each session and leaves the Mac unlocked meanwhile.
The probe drives the app through FieldNotesApp with isolated storage; a plain app build smoke (A15, M15) is needed to confirm real startup, permissions and storage.
The test kit lives outside the repo at ~/.mitosis/field-notes/testkit; the Swift helpers must be compiled there and the patches applied to fresh scratch worktrees each session.

The phone has a secure lock (PIN or pattern). The agent never enters it, so any screen-off outside the probe needs the owner to unlock. The probe's FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON covers only its own window; the F24 watcher (scratchpad keepawake.zsh, pokes after 15 s idle when the probe is not in front) kept the screen on all session without changing any setting.

adb input text (and hardware keyboards) take a different editor path from the Samsung soft keyboard: B3 (photo deletion) happens only on the key path, while H4 and H12 were confirmed with real soft-keyboard taps. Judge input-path defects with both paths before recording them.

key_decisions.title: Live-test input never leaves the device under test
Normal-user journeys with small samples; Android first, macOS on permission
Harness may grant the Android probe every runtime permission
Keep the phone awake with an F24 user-activity watcher, not the Stay awake setting
Spec and implement the Android fixes before macOS testing
key_decisions.scope: Thread sequencing after the Android report

out_of_scope.text: Full-count 6.14 gate runs (10,000 fuzz sequences, 20 clicks per hold, 500-click sweeps); they belong to the pre-merge gate run after fixes
Fixing the defects found; this thread tests and reports, fixes are separate work
iOS, and the sync or pairing placeholder in Settings
Committing the test kit, scratch patches or drive.sh harness fixes to the repo without the owner's go-ahead
Changing system settings on the Mac or the phone without asking
